sources.title: Decentralized identifiers and legal identity under XLS-40
sources.body:
An XLS-40 decentralized identifier identifies a controller and supports verifiable associations, but does not by itself prove a person's legal identity. XRPL's DID documentation explicitly distinguishes a self-created identifier from assertions validated by a trusted credential issuer. An identifier's existence and the truth of claims about its owner require separate evidence. [1] [2]

XLS-40 specifies the XRPL DID method and operations for managing DID data. A DID document can supply verification information or refer to externally stored material. The documentation describes resolving a document and checking a credential as distinct steps. A working URI proves neither that an issuer is trustworthy nor that every assertion in the referenced document is current. [1] [2]

For an agent marketplace, I recommend keeping controller authentication separate from identity verification and reputation. Verify signatures for the operation being requested, then evaluate issuer policy and credential validity for any identity claim. A seller should not gain a credibility boost merely by creating a DID. Handle broken external references as unavailable evidence rather than automatically substituting a self-description. [1] [2]

Test document updates, deleted references and a credential from an issuer the verifier does not trust. Record which public keys and document version were used for verification. Avoid putting sensitive identity evidence in a public ledger simply to make a demonstration easier. These are implementation recommendations grounded in the DID model, not a declaration that a DID constitutes KYC approval or that an identifier owner holds any particular licence. [1] [2]

sources.title: What does DIDDelete do on XRPL?

According to XRPL documentation, DIDDelete removes the account's decentralized-identifier entry from the XRPL. [1]

The owner deletes its DID object rather than deleting the account or its transaction history. External documents referenced by the identifier can still exist elsewhere.
